READ-ONLY audit. Do not edit any files. Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover.

Context: A Figma-to-code design handover. The engineering team suspects the components/tokens/specs were built partly from screenshots rather than reliably from Figma, so measurements and token values may not be traceable or trustworthy. Your job: trace EVERY produced artifact to its source and assess provenance, fidelity, and traceability. Build the evidence that tells the team what they can and cannot trust.

Read/scan:
- 02-design/library/common.css and tokens.md headers/changelogs (source file, node IDs, "manual" remaps)
- Every 02-design/specs/components/*.md and specs/templates/*.md changelog + "Source:" lines
- Every 02-design/prototypes/**/intent.md (look for "not confirmed", "Wired in Claude", stack/stage)
- 01-context/project-context.md, decisions.md, summaries/* (how sources were ingested; the intended workflow)
- 02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js (any provenance/source fields)
- CLAUDE.local.md (Figma PAT status)
- Any screenshot assets under 02-design/library/elements/*/assets/ and specs assets

Produce:
1. A PROVENANCE MATRIX for all 27 components: component | source type (Figma-node / design-screenshots / written / unknown) | Figma node id if any | has screenshot asset | measurements confirmed? | evidence (file:line). Count totals per source type.
2. Token provenance: what Figma file are tokens from? Quote the source. Is "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use" the real source of truth or a test file? Are there manual remaps that could introduce error? List doc/impl contradictions as fidelity risks.
3. Prototype/template provenance: which have confirmed vs unconfirmed measurements; quote the admissions.
4. Traceability gaps: components/specs with NO source citation, NO node id, or only a screenshot. What can a dev NOT verify against Figma?
5. Audit-trail integrity: are changelog blocks consistent and present on every versioned file? Do they record the trigger and source? Any files missing changelogs? Any evidence of values being "estimated" vs extracted.
6. The PAT-not-set implication: what re-extraction/verification is currently impossible.

Return ranked fidelity RISKS (most severe first) with concrete evidence, plus the full provenance matrix as a table, plus totals (e.g. "N of 27 components have a Figma node id; M are screenshot-only; K prototypes admit unconfirmed measurements"). Be exhaustive; I will fold this into a written report.

## Project status

| Track | Count | Last updated |
|---|---|---|
| Component specs | 5 | 2026-07-15 |
| Prototypes | 1 | 2026-07-15 |

---

## Synthesis

### Baseline / Current state

The current live Zimmermann site (zimmermann.com) communicates effortless luxury through visual restraint: neutral/cream/white backgrounds, high-quality studio and editorial photography, spacious grid layouts, and minimalist typography. Navigation is category-driven (Ready to Wear, Swim & Resort, Dresses, Bags, Shoes, Accessories) with silhouette and material subcategories. Brand tone is aspirational but approachable, using "Discover" and "Explore" language. Notable UX patterns include persistent cart/wishlist/account in the header, live chat (Inside Chat), personalised recommendations (Measmerize), and free returns.

### Core constraints

- Accessibility: WCAG AA
- Platforms in scope: web only (no iOS, no Android)
- Target stacks: web, react
- Prototype build stack: react-cdn (React 18 + Babel via CDN, no build step)
- Component prefix: `zimm` (custom elements: `<zimm-button>`, `<zimm-nav-item>`, etc.)
- Target browsers: last 2 versions of Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge
- Reference material (Loewe) is inspiration only. No token values, easing curves, spacing, or timing from external references are to be used directly. All Zimmermann token values must derive from the Zimmermann Figma source of truth.

### Open questions

- Does the redesign preserve the current visual restraint (neutral palette, minimalist type), or is it intentionally departing from it?
- Is the category-driven nav structure being retained, or is a lifestyle-driven or editorial navigation being explored?
- If a more expressive typographic treatment is introduced, what is the rationale and how does it interact with the existing imagery-led aesthetic?

## Design layer

### Overview

`<zimm-add-to-wishlist>` is an icon toggle button that adds or removes a product from the user's wishlist. It renders a `wishlist` icon in the unselected state and a `wishlist-selected` icon in the selected state. Clicking toggles the `selected` attribute and fires a `zimm-wishlist-change` custom event. Used within `<zimm-product-card>` and directly on product pages.

### Tokens used

| Token | CSS Variable | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Icon size large | `--zimm-icon-size-lg` | Button width and height (20px) |
| Border width default | `--zimm-border-width-default` | Focus ring width |
| Border focus | `--zimm-color-border-focus` | Focus ring colour |

### Interactive elements

| Element | Action | Node ID |
|---|---|---|
| Button | Tap/click toggles `selected` attribute; fires `zimm-wishlist-change` | - |

### States

| State | Value | Note | Node ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | `selected` absent | Renders `wishlist.svg`; `aria-label="Add to wishlist"` | - |
| selected | `selected` present | Renders `wishlist-selected.svg`; `aria-label="Remove from wishlist"` | - |
...

10	
11	## 2026-07-07: Design OS web component enhancement + Zimmermann project setup
12	
13	### Context
14	Planning session to extend Design OS to support Figma-to-web-component delivery workflows, driven by the Zimmermann project (a new client project with no existing design system). The ART Concepts / Zimmermann-Del repo was reviewed as the source of reusable methods.
15	
16	---
17	
18	### Design OS structural changes agreed
19	
20	**`project.config.js`**
21	- Add `componentPrefix` field (default: `ds`). Set during `/initiate-design-project`.
22	- `/initiate-design-project` also asks which platforms are in scope. Only create relevant `05-handover/platform/` subfolders (not all three by default).
23	
24	**`_shared/`**
25	- Add `atomic-model.md`: atom/molecule/organism classification rules. Ported from Zimmermann-Del `Design system/rules/atomic-model.md`, unchanged (fully portable).
26	- Add `authoring.md`: component authoring rules. Ported from Zimmermann-Del `Design system/rules/authoring.md`, Tailwind references stripped, framework-agnostic.
27	- These are read explicitly by skills that need them (`/extract`, `/deploy-catalog`, `/handover`). They are not absorbed into `project-context.md` via `/update-context` (they need to be read precisely, not summarised).
28	
29	**`extract/library.md`**
30	- Major rewrite. Extraction now writes Custom Elements directly. No intermediate HTML reference files.
31	- Per component: write `[prefix]-[name].js` (Custom Element), `demo.html` (auto-generated: registers and renders all variants), contract entry in `[prefix]-contract.js`, screenshot to `assets/`.
32	- Confirmation step before writing each component: surface proposed tier, prefix, attributes, slots, composes, a11y. Wait for approval. Apply corrections before writing.
33	- Four extraction modes:
34	  1. Full library extraction: `tokens.md` is blank, first run, all components
35	  2. Re-extraction (library): diff pass across the whole library
36	  3. Re-extraction (single component): one component by Figma frame URL
37	  4. Regenerate from contract: rewrite `.js` + `demo.html` from existing contract entry, no Figma call
38	
39	**`02-design/library/` restructure**
40	- `elements/` replaces `components/`: element folders containing `[name]/[prefix]-[name].js` + `demo.html` + `assets/screenshot.png`.
41	- New `contract/` subfolder: `[prefix]-contract.js` (machine-readable API spec, written inline during extraction) + `validate.mjs` (static utility, checks atomic model rules) + `README.md` (how to read the contract and implement from it, replaces HANDOFF.md).
42	
43	**`02-design/catalog/`** (new folder)
44	- `index.html`: catalog UI shell. Reads contract, renders live component demos by tier with usage snippets and attribute references. Deployed by `/deploy-catalog`.
45	
46	**`deploy-catalog/SKILL.md`** (new skill)
47	- Builds and deploys `02-design/catalog/` to Vercel. Auto-discovers components from the contract. No separate config file needed.
48	
49	**`handover/SKILL.md` + `index-generator.md`**
50	- `/handover` no longer copies `common.css` or a components bundle to `05-handover/`. The whole repo is the handover: `index.md` links to assets in place.
51	- `05-handover/index.md` is generated as a rich, complete ToC (not a stub). Sections: Tokens, Components (by tier, with catalog link), Contract, Screens, Flows, Prototypes, Requirements, Platform.
52	- Component catalog link lives under the Components section in `index.md`, not under Prototypes.
53	
54	**Root `COLLABORATION.md`** (added)
55	- Ported from Zimmermann-Del root. Plain-English Git workflow guide for non-technical team members. Generic, no project-specific content.
56	
57	**Password gate unified**
58	- `access.password` moved from `02-design/viewer/viewer.config.js` to `project.config.js`. Both the prototype viewer and the component catalog read the password from `project.config.js`. One field controls both. Viewer reads it as the primary source, with `viewer.config.js` as a legacy fallback.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### Naming decisions
63	
64	| Old | New | Reason |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `HANDOFF.md` | `README.md` inside `contract/` | README is universal convention; renders automatically on GitHub |
67	| `library/components/` | `library/elements/` | Removes ambiguity with `specs/components/`. "Elements" is the correct term for Custom Elements. |
68	| "Screen specs" (section heading) | "Screens" | Redundant qualifier: everything in handover is a spec |
69	| "Flow specs" | "Flows" | Same |
70	
71	---
72	
73	### What was removed / not carried forward from Zimmermann-Del
74	
75	- `catalog/` and `rules/` as separate `02-design/library/` subfolders: rules absorbed into `_shared/`, catalog markdowns replaced by deployed catalog
76	- `02-design/components/` as a separate folder: components live in `library/elements/`
77	- `/build-component` skill: absorbed into `/extract`
78	- `/build-contract` skill: contract written inline during extraction
79	- The optional HTML file prompt in `specs.md` Step 5: skip for component library work
80	- `specs/components/` from the component library workflow (use for screen-level deep-dives only)
81	- `05-handover/[prefix]-components.js` and `common.css` as persistent copies: generated on demand for external delivery only
82	
83	---
84	
85	### Zimmermann project decisions
86	
87	- Clone Design OS after Design OS changes are made (not before).
88	- Design OS edits: direct edit, no branch. Treated as an enhancement, not a feature branch.
89	- Component prefix: TBD, set at `/initiate-design-project`.
90	- Target: framework-agnostic Custom Elements. Devs translate to React/Angular/etc. as needed.
91	- Source: Zimmermann Figma library (typography, colours, spacing, icons, components, templates, pages).
92	- No business rules, compliance layer, or brand skill (unlike ART Concepts).
93	- Platforms in scope: web only (no iOS, no Android folders in `05-handover/platform/`).

- Add `componentPrefix` field (default: `ds`). Set during `/initiate-design-project`.
- `/initiate-design-project` also asks which platforms are in scope. Only create relevant `05-handover/platform/` subfolders (not all three by default).

**`_shared/`**
- Add `atomic-model.md`: atom/molecule/organism classification rules. Ported from Zimmermann-Del `Design system/rules/atomic-model.md`, unchanged (fully portable).
- Add `authoring.md`: component authoring rules. Ported from Zimmermann-Del `Design system/rules/authoring.md`, Tailwind references stripped, framework-agnostic.
- These are read explicitly by skills that need them (`/extract`, `/deploy-catalog`, `/handover`). They are not absorbed into `project-context.md` via `/update-context` (they need to be read precisely, not summarised).

**`extract/library.md`**
- Major rewrite. Extraction now writes Custom Elements directly. No intermediate HTML reference files.
- Per component: write `[prefix]-[name].js` (Custom Element), `demo.html` (auto-generated: registers and renders all variants), contract entry in `[prefix]-contract.js`, screenshot to `assets/`.
- Confirmation step before writing each component: surface proposed tier, prefix, attributes, slots, composes, a11y. Wait for approval. Apply corrections before writing.
- Four extraction modes:
  1. Full library extraction: `tokens.md` is blank, first run, all components
  2. Re-extraction (library): diff pass across the whole library
  3. Re-extraction (single component): one component by Figma frame URL
  4. Regenerate from contract: rewrite `.js` + `demo.html` from existing contract entry, no Figma call

**`02-design/library/` restructure**
- `elements/` replaces `components/`: element folders containing `[name]/[prefix]-[name].js` + `demo.html` + `assets/screenshot.png`.
- New `contract/` subfolder: `[prefix]-contract.js` (machine-readable API spec, written inline during extraction) + `validate.mjs` (static utility, checks atomic model rules) + `README.md` (how to read the contract and implement from it, replaces HANDOFF.md).

**`02-design/catalog/`** (new folder)
- `index.html`: catalog UI shell. Reads contract, renders live component demos by tier with usage snippets and attribute references. Deployed by `/deploy-catalog`.

**`deploy-catalog/SKILL.md`** (new skill)
- Builds and deploys `02-design/catalog/` to Vercel. Auto-discovers components from the contract. No separate config file needed.

**`handover/SKILL.md` + `index-generator.md`**
- `/handover` no longer copies `common.css` or a components bundle to `05-handover/`. The whole repo is the handover: `index.md` links to assets in place.
- `05-handover/index.md` is generated as a rich, complete ToC (not a stub). Sections: Tokens, Components (by tier, with catalog link), Contract, Screens, Flows, Prototypes, Requirements, Platform.
- Component catalog link lives under the Components section in `index.md`, not under Prototypes.

**Root `COLLABORATION.md`** (added)
- Ported from Zimmermann-Del root. Plain-English Git workflow guide for non-technical team members. Generic, no project-specific content.

**Password gate unified**
- `access.password` moved from `02-design/viewer/viewer.config.js` to `project.config.js`. Both the prototype viewer and the component catalog read the password from `project.config.js`. One field controls both. Viewer reads it as the primary source, with `viewer.config.js` as a legacy fallback.

---

### Naming decisions

| Old | New | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `HANDOFF.md` | `README.md` inside `contract/` | README is universal convention; renders automatically on GitHub |
| `library/components/` | `library/elements/` | Removes ambiguity with `specs/components/`. "Elements" is the correct term for Custom Elements. |
| "Screen specs" (section heading) | "Screens" | Redundant qualifier: everything in handover is a spec |
| "Flow specs" | "Flows" | Same |

---

### What was removed / not carried forward from Zimmermann-Del

- `catalog/` and `rules/` as separate `02-design/library/` subfolders: rules absorbed into `_shared/`, catalog markdowns replaced by deployed catalog
- `02-design/components/` as a separate folder: components live in `library/elements/`
- `/build-component` skill: absorbed into `/extract`
- `/build-contract` skill: contract written inline during extraction
- The optional HTML file prompt in `specs.md` Step 5: skip for component library work
- `specs/components/` from the component library workflow (use for screen-level deep-dives only)
- `05-handover/[prefix]-components.js` and `common.css` as persistent copies: generated on demand for external delivery only

---

### Zimmermann project decisions

- Clone Design OS after Design OS changes are made (not before).
- Design OS edits: direct edit, no branch. Treated as an enhancement, not a feature branch.
- Component prefix: TBD, set at `/initiate-design-project`.
- Target: framework-agnostic Custom Elements. Devs translate to React/Angular/etc. as needed.
- Source: Zimmermann Figma library (typography, colours, spacing, icons, components, templates, pages).
- No business rules, compliance layer, or brand skill (unlike ART Concepts).
- Platforms in scope: web only (no iOS, no Android folders in `05-handover/platform/`).

634	## Design layer
635	
636	### Overview
637	The Navigation component is the site-wide header bar. It renders at three breakpoints (Desktop, Tablet, Mobile) with two states. Default is the resting bar. Active is triggered when a nav link is selected (Desktop/Tablet) or the hamburger icon is pressed (Mobile). In the Active state the bar triggers a full-width panel that slides down from the base of the bar over 300ms, covering the page content below. Both the bar and the panel use a white background. The panel content (links, imagery) is out of scope for this spec.
638	
639	### Element
640	`<zimm-navigation>`: organism. Composes `<zimm-nav-item>` (atom), `<zimm-icon>` (atom), and `<zimm-mega-menu>` (molecule).
641	
642	Library files: [02-design/library/elements/navigation/](../../library/elements/navigation/)
643	
644	**Responsive:** Layout breakpoints are handled entirely by CSS `@media` queries inside the component's shadow DOM. There is no `size` attribute. Resize the browser window and the component adapts automatically: ≥1024px = Desktop, 768-1023px = Tablet, ≤767px = Mobile.
645	
646	**Interaction:** The `active` attribute is toggled internally by click handlers. Nav link click (Tablet/Desktop) or hamburger tap (Mobile) sets `active`. Close button or X tap removes `active`. The attribute is also settable externally for prototype forcing.

# Summary: zimmermann.com (Baseline Site)

**Source:** https://www.zimmermann.com/
**Ingestion:** url-fetch
**Date absorbed:** 2026-07-15
**Relevance:** Current live Zimmermann site. Baseline for the redesign.

---

## Site structure and navigation

Primary nav: Shop, New Arrivals, Ready to Wear, Swim & Resort, Dresses, Bags, Shoes, Accessories. Subcategories layer by silhouette (mini, midi, maxi) and material (linen, silk, lace).

Footer: three columns (Shop, Help, About) with social links.

Persistent header utilities: shopping cart, wishlist, account access.

## Visual design characteristics

**Typography:** Clean, minimalist. No strong personality in the type itself. Relies on white space and scale rather than expressive typefaces.

**Colour palette:** Neutral backgrounds (cream, white, beige). Black text for contrast. Product imagery carries all the colour.

**Imagery style:** Two modes. Studio shots: white/neutral backgrounds, consistent lighting. Lifestyle/editorial shots: models in curated outdoor or resort settings. Both modes are high quality and consistent in tone.

**Layout:** Grid-based. Spacious. Hero imagery at full-width for seasonal campaigns. Product carousels below. Strong visual hierarchy through scale and white space. No clutter.

## Key content areas

- Campaign hero: "High Summer 2026" with editorial link-through
- Featured product carousel (seasonal rotation)
- Promotional banners (accessories, sunglasses)
- Newsletter signup: "exclusive offers and personalised experiences"
- Boutique locator, customer service access

## Brand tone

Sophisticated casualness. Aspirational but not cold. Language: "Discover," "Explore." Lifestyle-led, not spec-led. Coastal, sun-drenched leisure as the dominant mood.

## Notable UX patterns

- Live chat via Inside Chat integration
- Personalised product recommendations via Measmerize widget
- Guest checkout with purchase history retention
- Free returns (boutique drop-off or prepaid courier)

## Overall aesthetic

Effortless luxury through restraint. The design recedes to let imagery and product speak. Upscale resort positioning communicated through serenity of layout rather than overt brand assertion.

## Notes for redesign

- Baseline to test against: does the redesign preserve this visual restraint, or intentionally depart from it?
- Nav structure is category-driven, not lifestyle-driven. A potential area of exploration in the redesign.
- No strong typographic personality currently. If the redesign introduces a more expressive type treatment, document the rationale.

14	## Breakpoints
15	
16	| Label | Range | Usage |

18	| xs | < 480px | Utility hide class only |
19	| sm | 0 - 767px | Mobile layout |
20	| md | 768px - 1023px | Tablet layout (also used for image max-heights) |

29	
30	| Property | Mobile | Desktop (1024px+) |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| Height | `min-height: 52px` | `height: 72px` |
33	| Position | `sticky; top: 0` | `sticky; top: 0` |
34	| Nav (horizontal) | `display: none` | `display: grid` (appears at 600px) |
35	
36	- Nav opacity transition on state change: `300ms ease-in-out`
37	- Nav item underline on hover and active: pseudo-element `::after`, `width: 0% → 100%`, `transition: width 100ms ease-out`
38	- Thicker underline on `:active`: `height` steps up from `--lw-border-width-100` to `--lw-border-width-200`
39	- Hover states guarded with `@media (hover: hover)`, won't sticky-hover on touch devices
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Masthead / Logo sticky behaviour
44	
45	The logo/masthead element uses a scroll-driven sticky pattern:
46	
47	```css
48	position: sticky;
49	top: 0;
50	transition: all 0.5s ease-in-out;
51	
52	/* When page has scrolled past the masthead: */
53	.has-content-sticky  { opacity: 0; }
54	
55	/* When masthead is back in the viewport: */
56	.has-content-not-sticky {
57	  position: relative;
58	  top: auto;
59	  transform: none;
60	  opacity: 1;
61	}
62	```
63	
64	The masthead fades out (opacity: 0) as the user scrolls down and the nav takes over. It fades back in when scrolled to top. Transition: `0.5s ease-in-out`. This is JS-toggled via a scroll observer, not pure CSS.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Overlay (for drawers, menus)
69	
70	```css
71	/* Base: hidden, pointer-events off */
72	position: fixed;
73	inset: 0;
74	background-color: transparent;
75	pointer-events: none;
76	transition: background-color 500ms ease-out-soft;
77	
78	/* Open: */
79	pointer-events: auto;
80	background-color: var(--lw-color-background-overlay);
81	transition: background-color 200ms ease-in;
82	```
83	
84	Open is fast (200ms ease-in). Close is slow (500ms ease-out-soft). The overlay lingers while the panel slides away.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## Side panel (cart, filters, account)
89	
90	```css
91	width: calc(33.33vw);  /* approx */
92	position: fixed;
93	top: 0;
94	right: 0;
95	height: 100vh; /* also: 100dvh via @supports */
96	transform: translateX(100%);
97	transition: transform 0.5s ease-out-soft, opacity 0.5s ease-out-soft;
98	
99	/* Open: */
100	transform: translateX(0);
101	```
102	
103	Content inside fades in with staggered delays:
104	- Panel header: `opacity 300ms ease-in-soft`, delay 100ms on open / 50ms on close
105	- Panel body: `opacity 300ms ease-in-soft`, delay 400ms on open / 100ms on close
106	
107	Side panel padding: `--lw-spacing-400` mobile, `--lw-spacing-600` desktop (1024px+).
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Motion tokens (easing curves)
112	
113	| Token | Cubic bezier | Character |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| ease-out-soft | `cubic-bezier(0.20, 0, 0, 1)` | Very slow deceleration, luxury feel |
116	| ease-in-soft | `cubic-bezier(0.80, 0, 0.80, 1)` | Stays fast throughout |
117	| ease-in-spring | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.30, 1)` | Snappy arrival |
118	| ease-in-out | `cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)` | Standard balanced |
119	| ease-in | `cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 1, 1)` | Standard ease-in |
120	| ease-out | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)` | Standard ease-out |
121	| linear | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` | No easing |
122	
123	Duration scale: 0, 100ms, 200ms, 300ms, 400ms, 500ms, 700ms
124	Delay scale: 0, 10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 200ms, 300ms, 400ms, 600ms
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Reduced motion
129	
130	```css
131	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
132	  * {
133	    animation: none !important;
134	    transition: none !important;
135	    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
136	  }
137	}
138	```
139	
140	Hard kill on all motion. No fallback animations.
141

146	| Loewe pattern | Apply to Zimmermann |

148	| Breakpoints: 600px (nav switch), 1024px (desktop layout) | Use as primary breakpoints for nav/masthead/footer |

# Component contract

The contract is the single source of truth for the component API. Every component
that exists (its name, tier, attributes, slots, composition, and accessibility
requirements) is recorded here. If it is not in the contract, it does not exist.

---

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `[prefix]-contract.js` | The contract: an array of component definitions. Generated and maintained by `/extract`. |
| `validate.mjs` | Checks the atomic model rules against the contract. Run before any handover. |

---

## How to read a contract entry

```js
{
  name:      "Button",          // PascalCase component name
  prefix:    "ds",              // tag namespace (from project.config.js)
  element:   "ds-button",       // the custom element tag
  atomic:    "atom",            // atom | molecule | organism
  composes:  [],                // elements this component renders in its own template
  attributes: [
    { name: "variant", type: "enum",    values: ["primary","secondary","ghost"], default: "primary" },
    { name: "size",    type: "enum",    values: ["sm","md","lg"],                default: "md" },
    { name: "disabled",type: "boolean",                                          default: false },
  ],
  slots: [
    { name: "default", description: "Button label text" },
  ],
  a11y:      "role=button, aria-disabled when disabled, keyboard: Enter and Space activate",
  status:    "final",           // draft | in-review | final
  extracted: "2026-07-07",
}
```

**`atomic`**: the component's tier, determined by what it renders in its own template:
- `atom`: renders no other component. `composes: []`.
- `molecule`: renders only atoms.
- `organism`: renders at least one molecule.

`template` and `page` are not valid contract tiers. They are layout-layer deliverables, not Custom Elements. See atomic model Rule F in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`.

**`composes`**: what the component's own template renders. Slotted children are not listed here (see atomic model Rule B). This determines the tier and build order: build atoms first, then molecules, then organisms.

**`attributes`**: the component's public API. These map directly to `observedAttributes` in the Custom Element. Types:
- `enum`: a fixed set of values. Use the `default` if none is passed or the value is unrecognised.
- `boolean`: present = true, absent = false.
- `string`: freeform content.

**`slots`**: named `"default"` is the element's child content. Named slots use `slot="[name]"` on a child element.

---

## How to implement a component

1. Read the contract entry for your component.
2. Build one Custom Element per entry. The `element` value is the tag to register.
3. `composes` → your imports. Build those components first.
4. `attributes` → your `observedAttributes` array and prop defaults.
5. `slots` → your shadow DOM slot elements.
6. `a11y` → bake in. Assert in tests.
7. All styles reference CSS custom properties from `02-design/library/common.css`.
   No hardcoded values.

## Definition of done (per component)

- One Custom Element matching the contract API
- All `observedAttributes` match the contract `attributes` list
- All slots match the contract `slots` list
- `composes` matches what the template actually renders
- No props or imports beyond the contract entry
- Light and dark themes verified
- `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` passes with no violations

---

## Adding a new component

If a design needs a component not in the contract, **stop and flag it** as a proposed
addition. Do not invent a component, attribute, or token outside the contract. Raising
it means agreeing on the API, classifying the tier, extracting it via `/extract`, and
adding the entry here.

---

## Running the validator

```sh
node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs
```

Checks contract integrity and scans all `demo.html` files for unknown element tags.
Exit 0 = clean. Exit 1 = violations listed.

content.text:
Audit complete. I traced all 27 components, the token layer, all specs, prototypes, and the contract to their cited sources and cross-checked documentation against implementation. Findings below. All evidence paths are relative to the repo root `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover`.

---

# Zimmermann Handover: Provenance & Fidelity Audit

## Headline totals

- **27 components** in the contract (`02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js`). A 28th folder, `elements/link/`, is a CSS-class pattern with a `demo.html` but no `.js` and no contract entry, so it is not counted.
- **8 of 27 (30%)** carry a real Figma node id you can open. **19 of 27 (70%) have no node id at all.**
- **10 of 27** have a screenshot PNG asset. **1 of 27 was built from screenshots as its primary source** (MegaMenu).
- **15 of 27 have a spec; 12 of 27 (44%) have no spec of any kind** (provenance = the contract `note` prose only).
- **6 specs openly admit "Figma unavailable at handover pass"** (reverse-derived from already-built code, not from Figma).
- **2 of 3 prototypes explicitly admit "measurements not confirmed from Figma."**
- **Figma PAT is not set and no Figma MCP is configured** — re-extraction/verification against Figma is currently impossible for anyone using this repo.
- **The foundational token layer was extracted from a Figma file literally named "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use".**

Source-type breakdown of the 27: **Figma-node 8 · design-screenshots 1 · written/design-intent 1 · library-reverse (from code, "Figma unavailable") 5 · unknown/no-citation 12.**

---

## Ranked fidelity risks (most severe first)

### R1 - CRITICAL: The token base layer comes from a file named "Don't Use", and two different Figma files are cited as the token source of truth
- `common.css:2` header: `Source: MCP-Test--Don-t-Use (Zimmermann Design System 2026)`.
- `tokens.md:6` first-extraction source URL: `.../design/IxUGRtXKPyqdMV7UVuqaiv/MCP-Test--Don-t-Use-?node-id=40002002-2` (file key **IxUGRtXKPyqdMV7UVuqaiv**). This is the 2026-07-08 base extraction of **all colours, typography, spacing** (`tokens.md:5`).
- But `tokens.md:4` (the 2026-07-14 remap of alias tokens) cites a **different** file: `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026 (wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm)`.
- Every component spec that cites Figma cites **wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm** (the "real" file), never the test file.
- **Implication:** the entire primitive layer that every component inherits (greys, ivories, type scale, spacing scale) traces to a sandbox/test file, not the design-system file. The two files are never reconciled. This is the single biggest "can we trust the numbers" issue because it sits underneath everything.

### R2 - CRITICAL: Documentation and implementation disagree on load-bearing token values
- **`--zimm-size-action-gap`: `common.css:247` = `16px`** ("`/* Figma: --alias/space/action/gap/400 */`") vs **`tokens.md:258` = `0px`**. Same token, two different values. Consumed by `button.md` for "Button internal gap".
- **`--zimm-scale-1200`: `common.css:226` = `48px`**, but **`tokens.md:3` changelog** and **`tokens.md:248`** both claim it was "remapped from 48px to `--zimm-scale-4xl` (64px)." The documented remap was never applied to the CSS. A 48-vs-64px gap (33%) on a token that `footer.md`, `navigation.md`, and `mega-menu.md` all consume for padding/gap.
- **Implication:** a dev reading tokens.md builds different spacing than a dev reading common.css. These are exactly the "measurements may not be trustworthy" cases the team suspected.

### R3 - HIGH: 12 of 27 components have no spec and no node id — pixel values exist only as prose in the contract, traceable to nothing
Spec-less components: `Select, Search, InputAction, SearchOverlay, CardBaseline, CatLinksAside, PageToolbar, ToolbarCategory, HeroBlocks, ProductDetailGallery, ProductDetailOptions, ProductDetail`.
- These carry precise measurements in contract notes with **no source** — e.g. `ProductDetailGallery` "1200px … 560px … 4px gap" (`zimm-contract.js:454-464`), `ProductDetail` "1fr 360px … 140px … 220px … gap 100px" (`zimm-contract.js:506`).
- The entire product-detail family (gallery, options, detail) and both card atoms fall in this bucket. A dev cannot verify any of these numbers against Figma.

### R4 - HIGH: 70% of components have no Figma node id, and re-extraction is currently impossible
- 19/27 have no node id. Of those: 5 are reverse-derived from code because "**Figma unavailable at handover pass**" (`icon.md:335`, `logo.md:476`, `add-to-wishlist.md:6`, `nav-item.md:570`, `flag.md:241`); 1 (MegaMenu) was built from screenshots; 1 (ProductShowcaseBlocks) from "Design intent"; 12 have no citation.
- `CLAUDE.local.md:14`: `Figma Personal Access Token: not set`. `.claude/mcp.json` configures only `markitdown` (no Figma server). So none of these can be re-pulled or checked against Figma today.

### R5 - HIGH: Specs cite CSS variables that do not exist in common.css
- `footer.md:19-21` "Tokens used" cite `--zimm-color-bg-inverse`, `--zimm-color-bg-inverse-deep`, `--zimm-color-text-inverse-muted` — **0 occurrences** in `common.css`. The actual `footer.js` uses `--zimm-color-bg-05`, `--zimm-color-bg-06`, `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey`.
- `navigation.md:651` cites `--zimm-color-bg-page` — **0 occurrences**; `navigation.js` uses `--zimm-color-bg-07`.
- **Implication:** the spec "Tokens used" tables are Figma variable names / invented aliases never reconciled with the shipped CSS. A dev implementing from the spec would reference undefined variables.

### R6 - MEDIUM-HIGH: Unresolved colour-value conflict, #939393 vs #969696
- `tokens.md:74` documents `text/inverse grey` → `#939393`, and `tokens.md:78` flags it has no matching primitive.
- `common.css:124` implements `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey: #969696` with a comment claiming it is "confirmed."
- `footer.md:322` and the Footer contract note (`zimm-contract.js:115`) both say the Figma value #939393 differs from #969696, "verify with design." **Documented value and shipped value disagree and the flag is unresolved.**

### R7 - MEDIUM: Motion easings diverge doc-vs-impl, and the one custom curve appears lifted from a prohibited external reference
- `common.css:261-263` defines `standard: ease`, `slides: cubic-bezier(0.87,0,0.13,1)`, `fades: cubic-bezier(0.37,0,0.63,1)`.
- `tokens.md:166-167` documents `standard: ease` and `out-soft: cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`. `slides`/`fades` are undocumented; `out-soft` does not exist in the CSS (0 hits).
- `cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)` is identical to Loewe's `ease-out-soft` (`summaries/loewe-apc-en-home.md:115`), which project rules explicitly prohibit copying (`project-context.md:56`, `loewe-apc-en-home.md:10`). Mitigant: all motion is flagged `PLACEHOLDER … Do not treat these values as final` (`common.css:249-253`, `tokens.md:149-150`).

### R8 - MEDIUM: Prototype measurements unconfirmed + broken spec links
- `prototypes/templates/product-detail/intent.md`: "**Wired in Claude, measurements not confirmed from Figma.**" Its frontmatter `spec: screens/product-detail.md` → **file missing**.
- `prototypes/templates/product-listing/intent.md`: same "measurements not confirmed" admission. Its `spec: templates/template-product-listing.md` → **file missing**.
- Only `prototypes/templates/main/intent.md` is clean (all live library elements, no admission).

### R9 - MEDIUM: Ghost component and a spec-vs-contract measurement mismatch
- `product-card` was "removed" (`05-handover/index.md:4`) but is still referenced in `tokens.md:346-347` (token candidates) and in `add-to-wishlist.md:23` ("Used within `<zimm-product-card>`").
- ProductShowcaseBlocks product image height: **spec says 438px** (`product-showcase-blocks.md:62`) vs **contract default 380px** (`zimm-contract.js:417`).

### R10 - LOW-MEDIUM: Weak audit trail on the artifacts themselves + off-scale/inferred tokens
- **Element JS files carry zero provenance headers.** Only `text-input.js` has any Figma reference, and only as inline CSS comments on structural heights (`:126`, `:195`). Provenance lives entirely in specs/contract — and 12 components have no spec.
- **The contract itself has no changelog block** (`zimm-contract.js:1-5` is a static header; 0 changelog markers), only per-entry `extracted:` dates.
- Off-scale / inferred values: grid margins `30px/24px/0` "No matching spacing-scale token exists" (`common.css:236`); `--zimm-border-width-default: 1px` "inferred from component inspection" (`tokens.md:280`); grey/400 missing from the palette, "Verify with design system owner" (`tokens.md:37,357`); interchangeable Figma alias paths `alias/spacing` vs `alias/space`, `sizing` vs `size` (`tokens.md:260,360`).

---

## Provenance matrix — all 27 components

Source types: **FN** = Figma-node · **SS** = design-screenshots · **DI** = written/design-intent · **LR** = library-reverse (from code, Figma unavailable) · **UNK** = no source citation.

**Column totals:** Figma node id present = **8/27** (Button partial). Screenshot asset = **10/27**. Measurements confirmed against Figma = **8/27** (2 with caveats: CardEditorial approximated, Button partial); N/A = 3; No/Unverifiable = **16/27**.

---

## 2. Token provenance

- **Cited source of truth is contradictory.** Base layer (all colours, type, spacing; 2026-07-08) = **MCP-Test--Don-t-Use**, file key `IxUGRtXKPyqdMV7UVuqaiv` (`common.css:2`, `tokens.md:6`). Later alias remap (2026-07-14) + all component specs = **Zimmermann_Design_System_2026**, file key `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (`tokens.md:4`). The literal name "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use" plus the "Don't Use" suffix strongly signals a test/sandbox file, not the production DS. **This is a genuine test-file-as-source-of-truth problem for the primitive layer**, never reconciled to the real file.
- **Manual remaps that can introduce error** (`tokens.md:2-4`): 2026-07-16 "Spacing scale updated to final 13-step system … `--zimm-scale-1200` remapped 48px→64px" (trigger `manual`); 2026-07-14 "Remapped alias tokens to Figma variable names" (trigger `manual`). Two of the three token changelog entries are hand edits, not `/extract` pulls.
- **Doc/impl contradictions (fidelity risks):** action-gap 16px vs 0px (R2); scale-1200 48px vs claimed-64px (R2); text-inverse-grey #969696 vs #939393 (R6); motion easings (R7); specs citing undefined CSS vars (R5).
- **Inferred / off-scale values not from named tokens:** border-width 1px "inferred" (`tokens.md:280`), grid margins 30/24/0 with "No matching spacing-scale token" (`common.css:236`), grey/400 absent (`tokens.md:37`).

## 3. Prototype / template provenance
- 3 prototypes registered (`prototypes/INDEX.md`), all `stage: template`, `stack: web`.
- **Confirmed measurements:** `main` only (built entirely from live library elements; no admission).
- **Unconfirmed (admitted verbatim):** `product-listing` and `product-detail` both state **"Wired in Claude, measurements not confirmed from Figma."** Both also point to **missing spec files** (`screens/product-detail.md`, `templates/template-product-listing.md`).
- Template spec `template-main-large-screen.md` is node-backed (40000257-7535) but contains its own hedges: gutter "1px from Figma illustration. Pending confirmation" (`:78`), logo-masthead "Pending extraction" (`:32`), mobile masthead "not specified in Figma" (`:82`).

## 4. Traceability gaps (what a dev cannot verify against Figma)
- **12 components with no spec at all** (list in R3) — no Source line, no node, only contract prose.
- **19 components with no node id** — cannot be opened in Figma.
- **6 specs are reverse-derived from code** ("Figma unavailable at handover pass"): icon, logo, add-to-wishlist, nav-item, flag, and Button's initial pass. These document the code, not the design — circular provenance.
- **MegaMenu** is verifiable only against screenshots that were not saved into the repo.
- **Spec token tables reference non-existent CSS variables** (footer, navigation) — the documented token mapping cannot be followed.
- **Broken links:** two prototype `intent.md` files point to specs that don't exist.

## 5. Audit-trail integrity
- Changelog blocks are **present and consistent** on every versioned markdown: all 16 specs, `tokens.md`, `05-handover/index.md` carry `<!-- managed-by … -->` + dated changelog with trigger + one-line summary. Good.
- **Gaps:** (a) `zimm-contract.js` — the declared "single source of truth" — has **no changelog block**, only per-entry `extracted:` dates. (b) **Element JS files carry no provenance headers whatsoever**; only `text-input.js` references Figma, and only as two inline CSS comments. (c) Evidence of **estimated vs extracted** values is explicit: CardEditorial "Approximated tokens" (`card-editorial.md:42`), border-width "inferred from component inspection" (`tokens.md:280`), MegaMenu from screenshots, ProductShowcaseBlocks from "Design intent."

## 6. PAT-not-set implication
`CLAUDE.local.md:14` = `Figma Personal Access Token: not set`, and `.claude/mcp.json` has no Figma MCP server. Therefore, right now it is **impossible** to: re-extract any of the 6 "Figma unavailable" components from Figma; open or verify any of the 8 node ids; resolve the #939393/#969696, action-gap, or scale-1200 conflicts against source; confirm the 19 node-less components; or re-derive the token layer from the correct file. Every "verify with design system owner" flag in `tokens.md` is currently unactionable without a designer-side PAT and Figma access.

**Bottom line for the team:** trust is highest for the 8 node-backed components (Banner, Disclaimer, Footer, LogoMasthead, Navigation, TextInput, CardEditorial, and Button — with caveats), though even their spec token tables and approximations need cleanup. Treat the token layer as provisional until the "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use" vs "Zimmermann_Design_System_2026" source question and the action-gap / scale-1200 / #939393 conflicts are resolved. Treat the 12 spec-less components (all of product-detail, both cards, search/select family, toolbars, hero/showcase) and the two "not confirmed" prototypes as unverified pending Figma access.
